title: Mark 6:35-44 — Five Loaves and Two Fish
description: A cell fellowship study on Jesus feeding the five thousand — how God sees provision where we see shortage.
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: A great crowd followed Jesus to a deserted place. When evening came, the disciples saw only lack — no food and a late hour — and wanted to send the people away. Jesus challenged them: "You give them something to eat." They calculated the cost and focused on what they lacked. Jesus asked what they had. They found five loaves and two fish. Jesus commanded the crowd to sit in groups on the green grass, took the food, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples to distribute. They all ate and were filled, and twelve baskets of fragments remained.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: Human wisdom often focuses on limitations before possibilities — but God sees provision where we see shortage. Jesus did not ask what the disciples lacked; He asked what they had. Small resources in God's hands become sufficient when surrendered. God is a God of order: preparation often comes before provision. What is blessed by God becomes fruitful. God's provision is sufficient and overflows — with Him there is abundance, not merely survival. Nothing is impossible for Jesus; the size of the need does not limit God's power.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Faith begins where human ability ends. Jesus often stretches our faith beyond our resources. God is not looking for abundance in our hands — He is looking for surrender. Later, when the disciples were terrified on the sea, Jesus said, "Be of good cheer! It is I; do not be afraid." Mark tells us their hearts were hardened because they had not understood about the loaves. Miracles are meant to build trust, not just meet a momentary need.

discussionQuestions: Where do you tend to see shortage before you see God's provision?
What has God already placed in your hands that you may be overlooking?
What would it look like to surrender what you have to Jesus this week?
Why do you think the disciples' hearts were hardened even after seeing the miracle of the loaves?

quiz.question: What did the disciples want to do when evening came?
options: Send the crowd away to buy food
Pray on the mountain
Buy two hundred denarii of bread themselves
Leave Jesus and return to Capernaum
quiz.explanation: They saw only lack and wanted the people to go elsewhere.

quiz.question: How many loaves and fish did the disciples find?
options: Five loaves and two fish
Seven loaves and a few fish
Twelve loaves and no fish
Two loaves and five fish
quiz.explanation: Jesus started with what they already had.

quiz.question: What did Jesus do before the food was distributed?
options: He blessed and broke the loaves
He sent the crowd home
He bought bread from a village
He told the disciples to fast

quiz.question: How much food was left after everyone ate?
options: Twelve baskets of fragments
None at all
Five baskets
One basket
quiz.explanation: God's provision overflowed beyond the immediate need.

quiz.question: Why were the disciples' hearts hardened later on the sea?
options: They had not understood about the loaves
They had too much food
They refused to get in the boat
They did not see Jesus walking
quiz.explanation: Mark 6:52 connects their fear to missing the lesson of the miracle.
